title: Bài sưu tầm 328 - Passage 3: How Translation Shapes What We Call Literature
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 328

How Translation Shapes What We Call Literature

Paragraph 1. Readers who enjoy Fyodor Dostoevsky or Gabriel García Márquez in English rarely pause to consider that they are not reading the authors' own words, but those of a translator. In The Unseen Craft, literary scholar Elena Rostova observes that for centuries, Western publishing has prized 'transparency'—the illusion that a translated novel was originally written in the target language. When a translation reads smoothly, the translator disappears; when a sentence feels unfamiliar, readers blame the translator's lack of skill.

Paragraph 2. Rostova contrasts two opposing philosophies first outlined by nineteenth-century German thinker Friedrich Schleiermacher. The 'domesticating' approach smooths out foreign idioms, cultural references, and unusual rhythms so the book feels comfortably local to the reader. By contrast, 'foreignizing' translation deliberately preserves echoes of the source language's structure and cultural distance, reminding readers that they are encountering a voice from another place and time.

Paragraph 3. In the modern global market, however, economic pressures overwhelmingly favour domestication. Major publishing houses in London and New York translate a far smaller share of books than publishers in smaller European or Asian markets, and editors often reject manuscripts that sound 'too foreign' to English-speaking buyers. As a result, works from non-Western traditions are frequently trimmed or softened before publication, stripping away local humour and distinct narrative pacing so they fit familiar commercial moulds.

Paragraph 4. Rostova argues that this insistence on effortless fluency impoverishes world literature. Reading translated fiction should not feel like looking into a mirror that reflects only one's own habits; it should gently stretch a reader's ear. Encouraging bolder, less sanitized translations does not mean making books unreadable—it means trusting audiences to meet unfamiliar cultures halfway, rather than flattening every global voice into a single uniform style.

groups.title: Questions 27–32
groups.instructions:
Complete the summary using the list of words, A–J, below. Write the correct letter, A–J, in boxes 27–32 on your answer sheet.

A. resistance  |  B. invisible  |  C. commercial  |  D. diversity
E. approachable  |  F. altered  |  G. fluent  |  H. identity
I. historical  |  J. neglect
groups.template: In English-language publishing, successful translators are often expected to remain 27. {{q27}} by producing prose that sounds completely natural. This style, known as domestication, removes unfamiliar cultural details so that foreign texts feel 28. {{q28}} to local audiences. Conversely, a foreignizing approach tries to retain the original 29. {{q29}} of the source work. Because large publishers prioritize 30. {{q30}} appeal, translated books from outside the West are sometimes 31. {{q31}} to match domestic expectations. Elena Rostova contends that avoiding such uniform styles enriches literary 32. {{q32}} .

groups.title: Questions 33–36
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 328? In boxes 33–36 on your answer sheet, write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

groups.title: Questions 37–40
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D. Write the correct letter in boxes 37–40 on your answer sheet.

steps: Đoạn 1: the translator disappears ↔ remain invisible (B).
Đoạn 2: feels comfortably local to the reader ↔ feel approachable (E).
Đoạn 2: echoes of the source language's structure and cultural distance ↔ original identity (H).
Đoạn 3: economic pressures / commercial moulds ↔ commercial (C) appeal.
Đoạn 3: trimmed or softened before publication ↔ altered (F).
Đoạn 4: impoverishes world literature / flattening every global voice into a single uniform style ↔ enriches literary diversity (D).

q33.text: Readers usually notice a translator's work most when the prose feels awkward.

steps: Đoạn 1: Khi dịch trôi chảy, dịch giả 'biến mất'; khi câu chữ lạ lẫm, độc giả lập tức đổ lỗi cho tay nghề dịch giả.
Kết luận: Chọn YES.

q34.text: Friedrich Schleiermacher personally preferred the domesticating method of translation.

steps: Đoạn 2: Chỉ nói Schleiermacher vạch ra 2 trường phái đối lập, hoàn toàn không nêu ông thích trường phái nào hơn.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q35.text: English-language publishers release a higher proportion of translated books than publishers in smaller countries.

steps: Đoạn 3: "translate a far smaller share of books than publishers in smaller European or Asian markets" (tỷ lệ thấp hơn nhiều, không phải cao hơn).
Kết luận: Chọn NO.

q36.text: Rostova believes that foreignizing translations are impossible for ordinary readers to enjoy.

steps: Đoạn 4: "does not mean making books unreadable—it means trusting audiences to meet unfamiliar cultures halfway".
Kết luận: Chọn NO.

q37.text: What is meant by 'transparency' in Western publishing in the first paragraph?
options: A. Publishers openly listing every editor who worked on a book
B. Translations reading as though no language change had occurred
C. Translators adding footnotes to explain difficult foreign idioms
D. Authors translating their own novels directly into English

steps: Đoạn 1: "the illusion that a translated novel was originally written in the target language."
Kết luận: Chọn B.

q38.text: How does a 'foreignizing' approach differ from domestication?
options: A. It updates nineteenth-century novels using modern slang.
B. It removes unusual sentence rhythms to improve clarity.
C. It keeps traces of the source text's distinct cultural voice.
D. It translates only the main plot rather than full chapters.

steps: Đoạn 2: Giữ lại dư âm cấu trúc ngôn ngữ gốc và khoảng cách văn hóa (preserves echoes of the source language's structure and cultural distance).
Kết luận: Chọn C.

q39.text: Why are non-Western manuscripts often modified before English publication?
options: A. Local authors request shorter chapters for digital editions.
B. Editors worry unfamiliar styles will hurt sales in English markets.
C. Translators struggle to understand regional humour accurately.
D. European publishing laws prohibit long descriptive passages.

steps: Đoạn 3: Biên tập viên thường từ chối bản thảo nghe 'quá ngoại lai' với người mua nói tiếng Anh để ép vào khuôn thương mại quen thuộc.
Kết luận: Chọn B.

q40.text: What is Rostova’s overall recommendation in the final paragraph?
options: A. Readers should learn foreign languages instead of relying on translations.
B. Literary awards should only be given to domesticated novels.
C. Publishers and readers should welcome translations that preserve cultural difference.
D. Translators should avoid working with commercial publishing houses.

steps: Đoạn 4: Khuyến khích bản dịch táo bạo hơn, tin tưởng độc giả sẵn sàng gặp gỡ các nền văn hóa lạ thay vì san phẳng mọi giọng văn.
Kết luận: Chọn C.
